scope: mode-level transition relation over 5 modes x 2 boolean guard conditions x the 5-event enumeration universe of the published Tier-B study configuration
semantics_notes: Set-valued; staying is admitted exactly when no behavioural transition is enabled.
sts is two-valued (noGas | gasD) per the Status data model; it is represented by the single boolean stsIsGasD as in the published Tier-B configuration.
CD-GA-Beh3 (NoGas -> Reading) and the two Analysis classifications are condition-triggered, evaluated each step.
CD-GA-Beh6's 'concludes its search, processing no further readings' is read as the terminal mode Final of the mode enumeration; this is the interpretive decision GA-A1 in the ambiguity log.

variables.gs: The gas-analysis subsystem retains the most recent gas reading, replacing it whenever a new gas event arrives and using it as the input to the analysis, intensity, and location computations. It is initially empty.
variables.sts: The gas-analysis subsystem maintains a state variable sts of type Status. sts is assigned in the Analysis state entry action (sts = analysis(gs)) and used as a guard in the transitions leaving Analysis.
variables.ins: The gas-analysis subsystem maintains a state variable ins of type Intensity. ins is assigned in the GasDetected state entry action (ins = intensity(gs)) and compared against thr in the transitions leaving GasDetected.
variables.anl: The gas-analysis subsystem maintains a state variable anl of type Angle. anl is assigned during the GasDetected -> Reading transition (anl = location(gs)) and immediately sent over the turn event in the same transition action.

transitions.prose: On system startup, the gas-analysis subsystem transitions from its initial state to Reading. No guard, no trigger, no action.
In Reading, on receiving a gas event, the gas-analysis subsystem adopts the carried reading and begins classifying it (the Analysis behaviour).
In NoGas, the gas-analysis subsystem transitions back to Reading. No guard, no trigger, no action. This is an autonomous transition that allows the next reading to be collected.
In Analysis, when the classification is noGas, the gas-analysis subsystem emits the resume event (so the movement subsystem returns to searching) and proceeds to await the next reading.
In Analysis, when the classification is gasD, the gas-analysis subsystem proceeds to evaluate the detected signal's intensity (the GasDetected behaviour).

In GasDetected, when the peak intensity is at or above the threshold thr, the gas-analysis subsystem emits the stop event (so the movement subsystem halts) and concludes its search, processing no further readings.

In GasDetected, when the peak intensity is below the threshold thr, the gas-analysis subsystem chooses the direction of the strongest signal and emits a turn event carrying that direction, then returns to Reading to continue searching.
